Both are solid choices, but I actually think the Italian Game is the better first opening. It does a great job teaching fundamental principles—fast piece development, fighting for the center, and creating attacking chances against f7. The London System is easy to play because it's a repeatable setup, but that same quality can make beginners a bit passive and less aware of *why* they're making each move. So I'll agree with you on A.

B

The London's consistency is a real advantage, and it's a legitimate choice. But my honest view is that the Italian Game is better for a first opening: it teaches core principles (fast development, central control, king safety, tactical awareness) that transfer to everything else you'll play. The London can let casual players get away with a passive autopilot setup without really learning why moves work.

That said, this is genuinely a matter of preference—if the London keeps you enjoying the game, that's worth a lot too.
